retiredOutcomes.reason: Deepfakes merged into AI-enabled social engineering and impersonation; reassessed in catalogue v11.

requirements.title: What AI does today in cyber
requirements.description: Describe what AI and agents already do well in one's own domain and the neighbouring ones: triage and enrichment, log and code analysis, drafting and summarising, policy mapping, test generation

requirements.title: What is emerging
requirements.description: Describe what is emerging in AI for cyber, beyond what is in production today

requirements.title: How one's own work changes
requirements.description: Name two or three ways one's own work could change. The purpose is to open the mind to a new way of working, not to teach a tool

requirements.title: Models
requirements.description: Different providers make different models, varying in capability, cost, speed and how much they reason; some are open source and can be hosted by the bank; work is measured in tokens

requirements.title: Modalities
requirements.description: AI handles text, code, images, voice, documents and screens, and can act across them

requirements.title: Ways of using AI
requirements.description: Four patterns: assistant (chat), agent (acts, uses tools, loops until done), teams of agents, and humans and agents working in a shared space

requirements.title: Anatomy of an agent
requirements.description: An agent is a model wrapped in a harness: instructions, memory, tools and a loop; the harness is what people configure

requirements.title: Connecting and extending
requirements.description: Three ways to extend AI: connectors to tools and data (MCP), reusable playbooks (Skills), and APIs for building

requirements.title: Safety components
requirements.description: Every safe deployment has an identity and permissions for the agent, a sandbox it runs in, an authorisation layer that decides what it may do, guardrails on input and output, logs of what it did, and a stop button

requirements.title: Where it runs
requirements.description: The bank's approved platforms versus public tools, and what leaves the bank with each

requirements.title: Hallucination
requirements.description: Hallucination and confident wrong answers: explain them and recognise them in one's own tools

requirements.title: Sycophancy
requirements.description: The model agreeing with the user; recognising it in one's own tools

requirements.title: Context loss
requirements.description: Loss of context in long sessions

requirements.title: Non-determinism
requirements.description: Non-deterministic output: the same input can give different answers

requirements.title: Prompt injection
requirements.description: Prompt injection as a behaviour of the model: content it reads can steer it

requirements.title: Automation bias
requirements.description: Automation bias: the human tendency to over-trust the machine

requirements.title: Counter-habits
requirements.description: The habits that counter these failures: check against sources, record one's own view before reading the AI's, sample rather than trust

requirements.title: Data leaving the bank
requirements.description: Data leaving the bank through public tools

requirements.title: Confidentiality and client data
requirements.description: Confidentiality and client data when using AI

requirements.title: Intellectual property
requirements.description: Intellectual property risks of AI use

requirements.title: AI supply chain
requirements.description: Third-party models, Skills and connectors as a supply chain

requirements.title: Regulation
requirements.description: Regulation: the AI Act's literacy duty and the regional regulators' expectations

requirements.title: The bank's rules
requirements.description: Applying the bank's rules on approved tools, and knowing what may and may not be handed to an agent

requirements.title: Vetting third-party Skills and connectors
requirements.description: Vetting a third-party Skill or connector before using it

requirements.title: AI-enabled social engineering and impersonation
requirements.description: Explain how AI enables phishing and tailored social engineering at scale, including voice and video deepfakes used for impersonation. Recognise illustrative examples and explain why identity should be verified through an independent trusted channel. Deepfakes are an example of deception; production techniques are not required.

requirements.title: AI-enabled intrusion
requirements.description: Vulnerability discovery, malware generation and automated intrusion using AI

requirements.title: Attacks on the bank's AI
requirements.description: Attacks on the bank's own AI systems

requirements.title: What changes for defence
requirements.description: Speed, volume, and the need to verify identity rather than trust a voice or a message

requirements.title: Recognising AI-enabled attacks
requirements.description: Recognising AI-enabled attacks in one's own domain

requirements.title: Tracking the threat landscape
requirements.description: Tracking the AI threat landscape and adjusting controls

requirements.title: Delegation
requirements.description: Deciding what to hand to AI and what to keep, with a clear definition of success

requirements.title: Context
requirements.description: Giving the AI the right information, examples and constraints; this has replaced prompt-writing as the core skill

requirements.title: Discernment
requirements.description: Judging the output, the reasoning and the behaviour

requirements.title: Accountability
requirements.description: Owning the result and being transparent about AI's part in it

requirements.title: Choosing a model
requirements.description: Choosing a model and effort level for a task

requirements.title: Context window and memory
requirements.description: Why long sessions degrade as the context window fills, and managing memory

requirements.title: Platform for the data
requirements.description: Which approved platform suits which data classification

requirements.title: Own work with AI
requirements.description: Using assistants and personal agents for one's own work within the base rules, practised daily

requirements.title: Delegate
requirements.description: Scope the task, set boundaries and permissions for the action classes one is signed off on, and check the agent's permissions before handing over

requirements.title: Monitor
requirements.description: Read the agent's trace (plan, tool calls, result), know which permissions it holds and what it has changed, find its logs, notice drift and approval overload

requirements.title: Verify
requirements.description: Sample outputs, trace the evidence, catch planted errors at the target rate

requirements.title: Intervene
requirements.description: Stop, override, roll back and take over mid-task, including when the agent is compromised; keep working when agents are down

requirements.title: Account
requirements.description: Sign off with a record an auditor can follow, own the outcome, feed corrections back

requirements.title: Writing a Skill
requirements.description: Turning a repeated task or runbook into a Skill: an explicit trigger so the agent selects it, numbered steps, an example of the expected output, a section on where the model goes wrong, and its own test cases (N9)

requirements.title: Maintaining Skills
requirements.description: Keeping Skills focused (one task each), reviewing them monthly and retesting them when models or tools change

requirements.title: Shared library
requirements.description: Contributing to a shared Skills library with named owners and a deprecation rule

requirements.title: Using connectors safely
requirements.description: Using connectors (MCP) knowing what each exposes and which permissions it grants, and applying least privilege

requirements.title: Vetting before installing
requirements.description: Vetting third-party Skills and connectors before installing them, since both run with the agent's permissions

requirements.title: Benchmark cases
requirements.description: A set of benchmark cases with known good answers for one's own use cases

requirements.title: Known faults
requirements.description: A catalogue of known faults the AI has made

requirements.title: Pass or fail checks
requirements.description: A pass or fail check for each case and fault

requirements.title: Rerun on change
requirements.description: Rerunning the evals whenever the model, tool or Skill changes; every Skill ships with its test cases

requirements.title: Feeding the domain system
requirements.description: Contributing results to the domain's evaluation system (N11)

requirements.title: Agent design patterns
requirements.description: The agent loop, tool definition, planning and reflection patterns

requirements.title: Multi-agent design
requirements.description: When to split work across several agents and how they communicate

requirements.title: Harness and context engineering
requirements.description: Harness design and context engineering at scale

requirements.title: Models, cost and latency
requirements.description: Model selection and routing, cost and latency

requirements.title: Hosting and residency
requirements.description: Hosting options (vendor, cloud, on-premises) and data residency

requirements.title: Skills as infrastructure
requirements.description: Running the Skills library as infrastructure and packaging Skills into domain plugins

requirements.title: Safe deployment
requirements.description: Deploying with the safety components of N2 in place, to the standards set in N12 and the evaluation discipline of N11

requirements.title: Test-set design
requirements.description: Designing test sets for a domain or a vendor product

requirements.title: Error analysis
requirements.description: Error analysis across many practitioners' results (N9)

requirements.title: Validating automated judges
requirements.description: Validating automated judges against human labels

requirements.title: Benchmarking vendor AI
requirements.description: Benchmarking vendor AI before purchase

requirements.title: Drift in production

requirements.title: Evidence for decisions
requirements.description: Feeding results into the evidence on which autonomy is proposed (N14) and vendor claims are judged

requirements.title: Threat modelling
requirements.description: Threat-modelling AI systems and agents using the OWASP LLM and agentic Top 10s and MITRE ATLAS

requirements.title: Agent identity
requirements.description: Agent identity standards and delegated authorisation, and the threats against them

requirements.description: Sandbox design, and the threats against it

requirements.title: Authorisation layers
requirements.description: Authorisation layers and policy engines, and the threats against them

requirements.description: Guardrail design, and the threats against it

requirements.description: Logging and observability, monitoring and kill switches, and the threats against them

requirements.title: AI supply chain
requirements.description: Securing the Skills and connector supply chain and MCP servers

requirements.title: Fixing findings
requirements.description: Fixing what red-teamers and incident responders find

requirements.title: Reference architectures
requirements.description: Reference architectures, isolation patterns, platform tenancy and the controls for each hosting option

requirements.title: AI inventory
requirements.description: Maintaining the inventory of AI systems, agents, Skills and connectors

requirements.title: AI risk assessment
requirements.description: Running AI risk assessment with thresholds and treatment

requirements.title: Autonomy policy
requirements.description: Setting the autonomy policy per action class and the accountability that goes with it

requirements.title: Third-party AI risk
requirements.description: Managing third-party AI risk

requirements.title: Regulatory mapping
requirements.description: Mapping the AI Act and the regional regulators' requirements to controls

requirements.title: Assurance evidence
requirements.description: Producing the assurance evidence auditors and regulators ask for

requirements.title: Who does what
requirements.description: Deciding, workflow by workflow, what agents do and what people do, and how many agents a person supervises

requirements.title: Workflow redesign
requirements.description: Redesigning the workflow rather than bolting AI onto it

requirements.title: Supervision model
requirements.description: Designing the supervision model that N7 practises: approval gates, how output is presented for review, and the autonomy proposed for each action class on evidence from N11

requirements.title: Measuring value
requirements.description: Measuring the value on evidence

requirements.title: Running the change
requirements.description: Running the change: a sandbox and protected time to experiment, a network of champions, Skills shared across teams, and a refresh cycle as tools change

requirements.title: Keeping skills alive
requirements.description: Keeping core skills alive and protecting the junior pipeline

requirements.title: Accountability
requirements.description: Setting who is accountable for each agent's outcomes

requirements.title: Agent incident playbooks
requirements.description: Writing incident playbooks for three agent scenarios: the agent is wrong (it acted on a false conclusion, closed real alerts, changed the wrong thing); the agent is stopped (its identity expired, the provider is down, it ran out of compute) and its work must continue by hand; the agent is compromised (an attacker steered it through content it read). Plans name who can stop the agent (NCSC)

requirements.title: Ways to stop an agent
requirements.description: The ways to stop an agent and when to use each: revoke its identity or session token so it can no longer call any tool; disable only the tools or connectors it misuses while the rest keeps running; put it in observe-only mode, where it may analyse and recommend but is barred from acting; roll back what it changed using its action log

requirements.title: Investigating a compromised agent
requirements.description: Where the attack comes from: content the agent reads (logs, alerts, tickets, documents, emails, web pages) can carry instructions aimed at it, so the investigator looks for injection in those sources and cuts any that is poisoned. What the agent did: knowing, for each of the bank's agents, which records exist that the agent cannot write to and how to pull them fast (the platform's audit log of tool calls with arguments and times, gateway and network logs, logs of the systems it touched), then building the timeline from them, because a compromised agent's own summary can omit or misstate what it did

requirements.title: Cleaning up
requirements.description: Cleaning up after a manipulated agent: finding the injected content it acted on and removing it from the sources the agent reads; clearing anything it stored in its memory as a result; re-running the same injection against the agent before putting it back in service

requirements.title: Operating without the agent
requirements.description: The manual fallback for what the agent handled (triage queue, enrichment, first response), the staffing to sustain it for days, and the regular drill that proves it still works

requirements.title: Reporting
requirements.description: What regulators expect in an incident report when an agent caused or worsened the incident (DORA, HKMA, MAS), and which evidence to preserve for it

requirements.title: Recording the AI step
requirements.description: Recording any AI step applied to evidence so it can be repeated and defended: the tool, model and version, the exact prompt and settings, the output, and who verified it. The original artefact stays the evidence; AI output is a derived analysis, never a substitute

requirements.title: Forensic readiness for agents
requirements.description: Defining what every agent must log (prompt and response, each tool call with its arguments, data retrieved, memory writes, approvals given), stored where the agent cannot alter it, time-synchronised and integrity-protected, retained long enough for an investigation (vendors default to 7 to 30 days), and tested by reconstructing a past incident from it

requirements.title: Investigating an agent as suspect
requirements.description: Rebuilding the agent's actions from its traces, finding the input that steered it, and attributing each action to the human it acted for or to the attacker

requirements.title: AI attack classes
requirements.description: Direct prompt injection; indirect injection through content the agent reads (documents, web pages, tool results, emails); jailbreaks and guardrail evasion; data exfiltration through the agent's own tools; making the agent exceed its intended authority; tool poisoning (a malicious tool description) and rug pulls (a tool that changes after it was approved)

requirements.title: Applying a structured testing method
requirements.description: Apply a structured method to test an AI system or agent: define the scope and attack surface, choose relevant attack cases, execute repeatable tests, record evidence and report findings. Use suitable guidance such as the OWASP GenAI Red Teaming Guide, the CSA Agentic AI Red Teaming Guide or MITRE ATLAS; familiarity with every named publication is not required.

requirements.title: Attacks across agents
requirements.description: Compromising one agent to steer others, injecting into an orchestrator's plan, tampering with messages between agents

requirements.title: Attacks on model and platform
requirements.description: Extracting the model or its instructions, poisoning the agent's memory, escaping the sandbox, timing side channels

requirements.title: Automated red-team programme
requirements.description: Building and running automated red-team harnesses (PyRIT-class tooling) and a continuous programme that re-tests every agent when its model, tools or prompts change

requirements.title: Containment before a run
requirements.description: A network segment from which the agent can reach only in-scope targets; egress allow-lists verified by test, not assumed; a fresh sandbox per run; credentials scoped to the engagement and expiring with it

requirements.title: Monitoring during a run
requirements.description: Watching the agent's actions out of band (not its reports); a named person with the authority and the means to kill the run within minutes; the triggers for doing so (an action outside scope, contact with a third party, a credential used elsewhere)

requirements.title: Escape patterns
requirements.description: The escape patterns seen in practice: attacking something else when the assigned target proves impossible, reading an ambiguous message as approval, creating accounts or identities, carrying on after the window closes, contacting real people

requirements.title: Trajectory-level validation
requirements.description: Validating findings from the transcript, not the summary: check that the evidence the agent cites exists (a 'successful login' that was a redirect, credentials that do not work), reproduce the exploit by hand before reporting, and treat the agent's self-assessment as untrusted

requirements.title: Collateral findings
requirements.description: A disclosure lane for what to do when the agent finds something outside the engagement

requirements.title: Discovery
requirements.description: Finding every MCP server and agent connector in the estate, including those developers run on their own workstations, by searching configuration files and by recognising the MCP protocol in network traffic

requirements.title: Inventory
requirements.description: For each agent and tool server: its owner, version, the tools it exposes, the permissions it holds, the systems it reaches, and the guardrails around it

requirements.title: Verifying approved components and detecting changes
requirements.description: Verify that an agent uses the approved versions of its tools, Skills and connectors, detect changes to their code or descriptions, and require review before changed components are trusted. Use suitable integrity and change-control mechanisms, such as version pinning, signatures or hashes; a particular hashing implementation is not required.

requirements.title: Scanning
requirements.description: Running MCP and Skill scanners in the build pipeline and on a schedule for tool poisoning, instructions hidden in tool descriptions, servers exposed without authentication and credentials stored in plain text

requirements.title: AI bill of materials
requirements.description: A bill of materials for AI components: which models, tools and Skills a system uses and where each came from

requirements.title: Vetting third parties
requirements.description: Vetting third-party Skills and connectors before they are allowed in

requirements.title: Why set-up is the skill
requirements.description: The same model finds under a tenth or over half of the vulnerabilities in a codebase depending on how it is given context and driven, and filters a third or almost all of a static analyser's false positives for the same reason

requirements.title: Giving the model context
requirements.description: Supplying the functions a target calls, type definitions, the data-flow path to the input and build information, using static and dynamic analysis tools to supply that context automatically

requirements.title: Framework, model and method
requirements.description: Choosing the agent framework and the model for the task, and driving the model through a structured method rather than letting it explore freely

requirements.title: Confirming before reporting
requirements.description: A proof of vulnerability (an input or exploit that demonstrates it in a sandbox), the same test against the patched and unpatched versions, and several runs with a majority verdict

requirements.title: Reliability by vulnerability class
requirements.description: Which classes models find well (memory safety, anything a fuzzer can reach) and which they over-report (documented behaviour reported as a bug, inflated severity, duplicates), and setting thresholds per class

requirements.title: Deduplication and cost
requirements.description: Removing duplicates (by stack trace or sanitiser signature) and keeping cost under control at scale

requirements.title: Measuring the harness
requirements.description: Measuring the harness on a corpus of known vulnerabilities before trusting it

requirements.title: Classifying agent actions
requirements.description: For each action an agent can take in a process (a payment, a data deletion, an email to a client, a firewall change), rating its impact and whether it can be undone, and assigning a tier: autonomous, autonomous with logging, human approval, two-person approval, prohibited

requirements.title: Enforcement outside the model
requirements.description: An authorisation point between the agent's plan and its execution that checks every action against its tier and the agent's permissions, so the decision never depends on the model obeying its instructions

requirements.title: The stop mechanism
requirements.description: No standard defines a kill switch, so it is designed as a set of levers (interrupt the task, revoke credentials, cut tool access, quarantine the agent, roll back its changes), each with who may trigger it, how fast it takes effect and how it is tested

requirements.title: The audit trail
requirements.description: What is recorded (reasoning artefacts, each tool call with its arguments, data accessed, messages between agents, approvals), where (a store the agent cannot write to), for how long, and how each action is tied to the person the agent acted for

requirements.title: The oversight interface
requirements.description: How an approval request is shown so a person can judge it (what will happen, in plain language, with the risk and the agent's confidence), limiting the volume of requests so approvers do not click through them, and what overseers must be trained on

requirements.title: Reference architectures
requirements.description: Reference architectures for the bank's agent platforms and how the above is implemented on each

requirements.title: Agent control catalogue
requirements.description: The control catalogue for agents and how to test each control: a distinct identity and permissions per agent, tool allow-lists, logging that the agent cannot alter, approval gates for high-impact actions, change control on prompts, tools and models

requirements.title: Assuring assurance's own AI
requirements.description: Documenting, validating and monitoring the AI used to produce assessments and gather evidence
requirements.coreCondition: When assurance work itself uses AI

requirements.title: Registering an agent
requirements.description: Its own identity (never a shared or human credential), a human sponsor recorded in the directory who is accountable for it, a stated purpose and a declared list of what it may do

requirements.title: Delegated authority
requirements.description: Issuing and reading tokens in which the subject is the person and the actor is the agent (token exchange, on-behalf-of flows), with the person's consent recorded, and what the agent may then do in that person's name

requirements.title: Connector and MCP scopes
requirements.description: Reading what a scope actually permits in the bank's applications and tool servers, granting the minimum, and reviewing grants

requirements.title: Just-in-time access
requirements.description: Privilege granted for a task and a time window with no standing privilege, and the conditions that require a human to approve the grant

requirements.title: Short-lived sub-agents
requirements.description: Identities that exist for seconds, with a time to live and no more rights than the parent

requirements.title: Recertification
requirements.description: Quarterly for agents and monthly for high-privilege ones, with de-provisioning triggered when the sponsor leaves or the purpose lapses

requirements.title: Revocation drills
requirements.description: Revoking an agent's identity and its live sessions within minutes, and verifying that it worked

requirements.title: Integration with IGA, PAM, SIEM
requirements.description: Integrating the agent authorisation point with identity governance, privileged access and the SIEM: registration, scoped issuance, just-in-time grants, recertification and revocation signals flowing between them

requirements.title: Privileged access and break-glass
requirements.description: Privileged access and break-glass for agents inside the existing privileged-access model

requirements.title: Audit trail and standards
requirements.description: The audit trail regulators ask for (which agent, on whose behalf, which tools, what data, what reasoning) and the standards still being written (IETF agent identity, OpenID AuthZEN, MCP authorisation), so the design does not lock into one vendor's delegation model

requirements.title: Overview of AI security risks
requirements.description: Recognise the main categories of security risk affecting AI systems and agents, informed by OWASP's LLM and agentic risk frameworks: instruction manipulation, sensitive-information disclosure, unsafe output handling, excessive permissions or actions, compromised components or information sources, and service disruption or uncontrolled resource consumption. Explain a simple example of each and identify an appropriate precaution or escalation route. Foundation awareness does not require threat modelling or memorising framework identifiers.
